inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Right Flipper Button (Lower and Upper Right)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 57 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 57: a host write to 57 is overwritten on the next update. This cabinet button drives both the lower-right and upper-right physical flippers while enabled. Manual PDF 40 braces both coil branches under Right Flipper: Orn-Vio at 1P19-1 feeds lower-right Blu-Vio and upper-right Blk-Yel (note 2: switch-to-coil). The retained script supplies separate lower/upper right callbacks through the flipper library; public output 34 remains unused.

mechanisms.behavior: Outhole and three-position ball trough feed the shooter lane.
mechanisms.label: Trough

mechanisms.behavior: Reset raises the left three drop targets; optos signal their matrix states.
mechanisms.label: Left Drop Bank

mechanisms.behavior: Reset raises the middle three drop targets; optos signal their matrix states.
mechanisms.label: Middle Drop Bank

mechanisms.behavior: Left Orion lock holds and releases a ball.
mechanisms.label: Left Lock

mechanisms.behavior: Right Orion lock holds and releases a ball.
mechanisms.label: Right Lock

mechanisms.behavior: Popper ejects a ball from the saucer.
mechanisms.label: Ball Popper

mechanisms.behavior: Controlled gate opens at the upper flipper.
mechanisms.label: Top Flipper Gate

mechanisms.behavior: Left outlane kicker returns the ball.
mechanisms.label: Left Outlane Kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower and one upper-right physical flippers are cabinet wired. The right cabinet button (input 82) drives both lower-right and upper-right flippers while enabled; the left button (84) drives the lower-left. Manual PDF 40 groups both right coil branches under the right switch. The VPX upper-right local callback 34 combines the key and game-on state; it is not a PinMAME output 34.
mechanisms.label: Flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Three C-12872 thumper bumper assemblies pair left, right and bottom switches 60/61/62 with coils 17/19/21; the coil returns the ball after skirt actuation. The physical trigger circuit and the ROM coil test establish the pairing; the driver leaves ssSw empty, so no switch-driven coil simulation is implied.
mechanisms.label: Jet Bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Each C-12873 slingshot has two physical leaf actuating switches sharing one matrix address (B-12459/B-12715). Left 63 and right 64 accompany special coils 18 and 20. Their switches release when the rubber returns; the VPX animation is implementation timing.
mechanisms.label: Slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Fixed ramp and crossover ball paths are sensed at Top of Ramp 17 and Transport 31. There is no independently driven transport motor in the factory inventory. The VPX speed-up helpers near 31 compensate its ball dynamics and publish no extra switch or mechanism mark.
mechanisms.label: Transport Ramp Path
